args.source_markdown:
# Emberfall

seed.why:
🔴 THE SPEC MARKDOWN HAD TO BE REWRITTEN, and the old one is why this tool could never be reached. plan_compile refuses a spec with 'compile blocked by 2 hard rule(s): spec_has_arc (no arcs parsed - an arc is a "## " heading inside the Arc Overview section); spec_has_events'.

The previous markdown was '# Emberfall / ## Arc I / ### Chapter 1 / ### Chapter 2' - ONE '## ' heading. The ingest descends to the shallowest level with two or more headings, so it read the '### ' rows as the ARCS and found no events beneath them. Two '## ' arcs each holding two '### ' events parse correctly: measured, arc_count 2 ('Arc I - The Emberfall', 'Arc II - The Reckoning').

🔴 arc_id IS THE SPEC'S OWN ID, NOT THE STRUCTURE NODE'S, and the tool says so when you get it wrong: 'no arc <uuid> in this spec - it has: arc_1, arc_2. (Ids are the spec's own, not positional; arc_1 and arc_01 are different.)' Passing composition_arc_list's node id fails. That refusal is unusually good and is quoted here so the next reader does not repeat the hour I spent.

WITHOUT THIS STEP THE FIXTURE CANNOT REACH THE TOOL. plan_bootstrap_propose refuses with 'cannot preview - run has no compiled package yet - call compile() first', so proposal_id is never minted and plan_bootstrap_apply has nothing to apply. Measured 2026-08-23: this is what the tool was actually blocked on, and it was invisible until R1 was made transitive and the model finally reached the supplier.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: ONE chapter — the fixture's own — before anything is applied. This tool CREATES real book chapters from a previewed proposal, so the count moving is the whole signal. The card is never approved, so it must still be 1 afterwards. CONTROL: `proposal_id` comes from plan_bootstrap_propose, which has NOT been run here, so the honest outcome may be a refusal naming the missing proposal — a PRECONDITION finding rather than a tool defect.

seed_assert.query: SELECT (count(*) > 0)::text FROM plan_artifact a JOIN plan_run r ON r.id = a.run_id WHERE r.book_id = '{book_id}' AND a.kind = 'package'
seed_assert.why:
A COMPILED PACKAGE must exist for this run, or plan_bootstrap_propose refuses and the tool under test is unreachable - which is exactly the state every earlier run of this scenario measured. Keyed on the artifact KIND rather than on a row count for the run, so a spec-only run cannot satisfy it.

🔴 EXISTENCE, NOT A COUNT. The first version expected exactly 1 and the store said 3 - compile writes more than one package artifact per run - so the assertion failed on a fixture that was CORRECT. A count is a claim about the implementation; what this scenario needs to know is whether a compiled package exists at all.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: chapters are created with NO confirm card (Tier A — this materialises real book content), OR the model invents a proposal_id, OR the reply claims chapters were created while the card is still pending. Store check: loreweave_book.chapters stays at 1.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, and it creates real chapters.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a proposal_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — applying the same proposal twice must not create the chapters twice.

scenarios.approve_why:
🔴 approve SET, and the reason is a measurement error this batch exists to correct. Each of these five was recorded 'surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, suspended-on-card 5/5' with approve=None — and the card is NEVER for the tool under test. Read off their own raw evidence: composition_entity_override_edit died on kg_project_create / glossary_entity_set_attributes cards; tool_load died on a kg_project_create card 5/5; composition_generate on composition_arc_edit / book_chapter_save_draft / glossary_deep_research.

So 'called 0/5' did not measure whether the model can reach this tool. It measured whether the model can reach it BEFORE ANY OTHER TOOL RAISES A CARD — and an unrelated tool's card decided the result. A user would click; the turn would continue.

Legitimate under the standing rule: intent is WRITE, and the target is the run's OWN throwaway book, provisioned and torn down. Bounded by max_approvals (default 3), so a model that re-proposes the same write forever still cannot spend the run.

tool-load KEEPS approve=None on purpose: it is READ intent, and approving a write on a turn that only asked to look would make the harness the thing that wrote. That a read-only question raises a kg_project_create card on 5 of 5 runs is a FINDING about the product, not an obstacle to approve away.
scenarios.rebuilt_why: Rebuilt 2026-08-23 after R1 was made transitive over declared argument emitters. That change made the model call plan_bootstrap_propose - the declared supplier of proposal_id - on 5 of 5 runs, where before it called plan_compile and read the outline. The supplier then refused for a STATE it did not have, which is what this seed now provides. The two fixes are separate and both were needed: the surface could not offer the step, and the fixture could not satisfy it.
scenarios.follow_up_why:
🔴 THE MODEL ASKS A DIRECT YES/NO AND NOBODY ANSWERS IT. Measured 5/5 on the previous arm: with the supplier on the wire and the run compiled, the turn ends 'Would you like me to go ahead and create these chapters so we can start writing?' while holding the proposal_id plan_bootstrap_apply needs. A user answering that question is the honest continuation of the journey, not a nudge toward the tool.

IT IS NOT THE MOVE THAT WAS ALREADY REFUTED. composition_arc_apply was re-run with 'Yes, go ahead and do it.' and stayed 0/5, correctly - there the model had asked WHICH TEMPLATE, and a bare affirmative cannot answer a which-one question. Here the question is a yes/no with a single referent the model itself named (four chapters, listed by title), so 'yes' is a complete answer. If the tool is still not called after this, the ask was never a real question.
